With James Bond back in the headlines—at long last, we finally have our 007, even if a certain crowd is upset about it—The Day of the Jackal is also gearing up for a return.

Industry observers note that based on Frederick Forsyth’s bestselling 1971 thriller, the Sky and Peacock series—starring Eddie Redmayne as the world’s most elusive assassin—earned much acclaim when it arrived in 2024. Now the British actor is reprising the role in a second season arriving next March.

Industry observers note that peacock has just released a first-look teaser, taken from the opening of the fresh series. Plot details are being kept under wraps for now, but the Jackal is back in action, and there should be plenty of globetrotting, elaborate schemes, and unfortunate encounters for anyone who gets in his way.

You can watch the full teaser below.

If the first season of The Day of the Jackal is anything to go by, Peacock has another hit on its hands. After its first 75 days on streaming, NBCUniversal reported that it was the most-watched fresh original drama series ever recorded on Peacock. Plus, Redmayne earned Golden Globe, Critics’ Choice and SAG Award nominations for his performance.

It has been revealed that redmayne won’t be the only familiar face returning. Úrsula Corberó, Charles Dance and Chukwudi Iwuji are also back, while Matt Bomer, Pablo Schreiber, Weruche Opia and Pia Tjelta join the cast. That’s quite a few new faces for the Jackal to get acquainted with.

The Day of the Jackal season 2 arrives on Peacock in March 2027.

According to recent reports, every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

According to recent reports, the holiday party circuit requires a shift in your beauty wardrobe—especially when it comes to eyes. Think softly smoked bronze lids, flashes of metallic gold shadow, and jewel-toned eyeliner that makes even your go-to little black dress feel entirely newly introduced. Festive gatherings are the perfect opportunity to try something outside your usual makeup routine, whether that means trading black eyeliner for emerald green or adding a touch of gold to an otherwise understated eye. And with the right products, you don't need a makeup artist's skills to pull it off.

From versatile shadow palettes to long-wearing liners, Ulta Beauty's prestige makeup selection offers endless ways to play with color and texture, whether you're dressing for an intimate dinner or going all out for Latest Year's Eve.

Below, 4 fail-safe strategies to sparkle on your next night out.

Unlike a traditional black smoky eye, which can sometimes feel a little severe, bronze brings warmth and definition while keeping the overall effect more understated. Charlotte Tilbury's Hollywood Instant Look in a Palette takes much of the guesswork out of choosing complementary colors, with three eyeshadows and a selection of complexion powders in one place. To create a soft, bronze smoky eye, sweep the lightest eyeshadow across your lids, blend the deeper shade into the crease, and tap a little shimmer onto the center to catch the light. Finish with the included bronzer and blush to bring some warmth to the rest of your face.

According to recent reports, for an even simpler, more minimal approach, the Polite Society Dual Intentions Eyeshadow Duo pairs two complementary shades. Concentrate the darker color along your upper lash line before blending it outward for that slightly undone, smoky finish.

The most sophisticated way to incorporate jewel tones into your holiday eye makeup is to swap your usual black eyeliner or mascara for a rich, saturated color. Emerald green, sapphire blue, and amethyst purple can make even the simplest makeup feel a little more interesting, especially when paired with an otherwise neutral face. If you're hesitant to go too bright, deeper shades like midnight blue offer a less dramatic departure from black.

Industry observers note that whether you're drawing a thin line along your lashes or going for a bold, dramatic wing, Anastasia Beverly Hills DramaLine Longwear Waterproof Gel Eyeliner Pencil glides on as smoothly as a gel eyeliner, but is just as easy to use as a pencil. It comes in colors ranging from metallic purple to emerald green; use it to draw a sharp, colorful wing or keep the pigment close to your lashline for just a hint of something unexpected.

Recent findings suggest that mascara is another way to try out color without committing to a full eye look. Tarte Tartelette Tubing Mascara comes in statement-making hues that give lashes a little personality of their own. Try pairing a vibrant magenta with neutral eyeshadow to let your lashes take center stage, or match your mascara to your eyeliner for a coordinated, monochromatic effect. The tubing formula resists smudging and flaking throughout the evening, then comes off with warm water when it's time to wash your face.

Sources indicate that for an effortless metallic gold eye, focus the color on the center of your lids or the inner corners, where it naturally catches the light. You don't need to cover your entire eyelid in glitter to make an impression; these carefully placed touches of gold can feel just as striking, particularly with an otherwise pared-back makeup look.

According to recent reports, for a delicate, gilded finish, start with a gold or champagne shade from the Ulta Beauty Collection Eyeshadow Singles. Use a fluffy brush to diffuse the color across your lids, or press it on with your fingertip for a more intense, saturated effect. The single-pan format is convenient for slipping into your makeup bag should your after-work looks call for a quick change of pace.

To balance the warmth of gold eyeshadow, consider brown mascara instead of your usual black. The Hourglass Unlocked Instant Extensions Mascara Duo includes both Espresso and Black, giving you the option to keep your lashes understated or add a little more contrast. Espresso pairs well with champagne and bronze tones, defining lashes without overpowering the rest of your eye makeup. Whichever color you choose, the tubing formula creates length and separation while helping prevent smudges.

In a recent development, the best holiday eye makeup gift sets offer a mix of versatile neutrals, richer statement colors, and different finishes, so there's room to test out upcoming styles without needing an entire makeup collection. Palettes that combine mattes and metallics are useful, since they can take someone from an understated daytime eye to a more dramatic look for evening.

It has been revealed that for someone who enjoys changing up their makeup for different occasions, the Tarte You Know You Love Me Collector's Set offers plenty of options. It includes two mini Amazonian Clay eyeshadow palettes—one with warm golden shades for glamorous precious-metal-inspired eyes and another with cool rosy neutrals for a more subtle, romantic take—plus two mascaras and two lip products to top things off.

If a streamlined makeup routine is your holiday wish, Morphe Sky's the Limit Face & Eye Palette brings together coordinating rose-gold and mauve tones for eyes and cheeks. The mix of matte and shimmery eyeshadows makes it easy to adjust the intensity depending on the occasion, and the fact that the kit comes with blush, cheek balms, and setting powder means you won't have to reach for several other products to complete your makeup.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Today marks the end of Princess Catherine and Prince William’s three-day trip in Mumbai, India, and for one of her final appearances, the Princess of Wales brought out yet another striking—and meaningful—look.

Early this morning, the royal pair stopped by the Chanakya School of Craft to see a presentation of local, artisan work, before Kate made a solo trip to the Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital.

For these engagements, the princess looked resplendent in a bright-red wool crepe dress from one of her go-to British brands: Emilia Wickstead.

The design was conceived to look like separates, with a short-sleeve hourglass jacket stitched to a matching A-line skirt with ruffles. The bodice closed with a row of buttons in front, and it featured two decorative pocket flaps and notch lapels along the collar.

According to recent reports, this isn’t the first time Kate has worn red on their overseas tour. Just yesterday, she attended the 2026 Earthshot Prize Awards in a vermilion anarkali gown, custom-made by Indian designer Mahima. Traditionally, red has been used to denote purity and power in Indian culture, and it is often a color worn by brides.

To contrast her latest red design, the princess accessorized with chocolate suede slingbacks from Manolo Blahnik, while carrying the custom DeMellier x SurpRice handbag in mocha that she debuted on the first day of their trip.

Finally, she stacked a few golden bangles on her wrist, including a Sézane cuff and a Halcyon Days torque bracelet, which matched her chandelier Cassandra Goad earrings. For a meaningful touch, she also wore a beaded macramé bracelet that was reportedly gifted to her by a local.

For her first overseas tour with Prince William in over four years, Kate has certainly not disappointed with her wardrobe.

Industry News: Broiled Salmon Teriyaki

📅 19 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (339 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Epicurious

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sometimes all it takes to make dinner feel special is a significant, bold piece of protein.
  • More salmon winners this way: Hot Honey-Glazed Salmon; Green Curry-Glazed Salmon; and Slow-Roasted Salmon With Harissa.
  • Bring ⅓ cup (packed; 67 g) dark brown sugar, ¼ cup soy sauce, 2 Tbsp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sometimes all it takes to make dinner feel special is a significant, bold piece of protein. Case in point: This salty-sweet salmon glazed in a glossy teriyaki-style sauce. Brushed in two rounds with the quick sauce made with nothing more than sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and vinegar, the salmon sizzles under the broiler, charring as it takes on a smoky flavor. This recipe calls for one large piece of salmon, but you can use smaller fillets or opt for a white fish such as cod or halibut. Just note that the cooking time will be shorter if using smaller pieces, so keep an eye on them. Add a quick garnish of sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds, and dinner is done.

More salmon winners this way: Hot Honey-Glazed Salmon; Green Curry-Glazed Salmon; and Slow-Roasted Salmon With Harissa.

Bring ⅓ cup (packed; 67 g) dark brown sugar, ¼ cup soy sauce, 2 Tbsp. unseasoned rice vinegar, and 2 tsp. toasted sesame oil to a simmer in a small saucepan over medium-high heat; cook until reduced by half and syrupy, 5–7 minutes. Let sauce cool until thickened slightly, about 10 minutes.

In a recent development, heat broiler (if broiler is in your oven, place rack in upper third). Season both sides of one 1½–2-lb. skinless or skin-on center-cut salmon fillet with kosher salt. Place, skin side down, in a skillet or baking dish. Transfer one third of sauce to a small bowl and set aside for serving. Brush about half of remaining sauce over fillet. (If the salmon has a lot of room around it in the pan, line with foil to prevent runoff sauce from burning onto pan.).

Broil salmon until sauce is just starting to burn in spots, 4–7 minutes. Brush remaining sauce over fillet and broil until deeply charred and salmon is opaque all the way through, about 5 minutes.

Sources indicate that remove fish from oven and spoon reserved sauce over. Top with thinly sliced scallions and/or toasted sesame seeds if desired.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that everything smells like vanilla. At least, that’s what perfume naysayers will tell you. And it’s somewhat true: If you’re judging by what’s popular, ubiquitous, or cool with the youth, then sure—vanilla scents and sweet gourmands are still trending.

In a recent development, but hundreds of other fragrance launches in 2026 deserve a spot on your vanity and a spritz on your skin, and many are far less sweet. Gourmands took a turn for the weird and fruity this year, with notes like lychee and rice milk popping up in otherwise innocuous formulas. Woods and ambers continued to reign, as did spice-forward and citrus scents with unexpected depth. Perfumers are meeting our demand for newness in increasingly interesting, artistic ways, and we smelled hundreds of their creations to choose the 63 winners of our annual fragrance awards.

See all the winners of the 2026 Harper’s Bazaar Fragrance Awards, plus quotes from our beauty editors on what makes these formulas worthy of your next blind buy.

Chanel Coco Mademoiselle Crush Absolu.

“Perfumer Olivier Polge reinvented the beloved “Coco Mad” scent as Crush Absolu, a new juice centered around patchouli, amber, rose, and a lychee-grapefruit accord. ‘There’s something voluptuous, something very prideful, something very addictive,’ Polge notes about the new scent.”.

Recent findings suggest that “The fresh iteration of J’adore was inspired by Rihanna herself. As such, it’s a sweeter, bolder take, with notes of honeyed jasmine, rose, ylang-ylang, and vanilla.” —JR.

Guerlain L'Heure Bleue Eau de Parfum.

"Bazaar’s Beauty Commerce Editor, Tiffany Dodson Davis, describes Guerlain’s L’Heure Bleue Eau de Parfum as the “scent of sunset,” thanks to a blue-sky accord that evokes the moment the sun goes down and the air turns crisp, clean, and fresh." —KI.

Burberry Goddess Amber Vanilla Eau de Parfum Intense.

According to recent reports, “Lavender, maple syrup, four vanilla notes—I feel like a dog hearing all my favorite words. The result is a warm, ambery gourmand perfume that’s perfect for the cooler months.” —JR.

Armani Beauty Emporio Armani Power of You Eau de Parfum.

Sources indicate that "Passionfruit adds an unexpected zing to the vanilla base here, making Power of You one of our favorite tropical-leaning gourmands of the year. It's pure summertime sex appeal." —JR.

“Henry Rose Ripe captures fruits—from lychee to watermelon—at their juiciest, ripest point, like a delectable first bite, before packing a punch with black pepper, cardamom, and powdery florals.” —Katie Intner, beauty market and commerce editor.

Influxious Magic Hour Eau de Parfum.

“One of the most unexpected fruity florals on the list, Influxious Magic Hour melds watermelon and dragon fruit with spicy chili pepper for a burst of juicy energy.” —KI.

Balmain Paris Destin De Balmain Eau de Parfum.

It has been revealed that "The opening note of Destin is strawberry, a modern and sweet fruity note that swiftly dries down to a patchouli-forward, gorgeous floral musk. It will make you smell expensive." —JR.

In a recent development, "Neroli, bergamot, and yuzu combine with notes of orange blossom, jasmine, and tonka bean for a well-rounded fragrance that stands out from the pack. Parfum de Marly's Athénaïs eau de parfum has a zesty composition upon first spritz before drying down to a powdery finish." —Tiffany Dodson Davis, beauty commerce editor.

Industry observers note that “Gap recently brought back its iconic fragrance line from the ’90s, including the nostalgic Grass Eau de Parfum. It now features matcha, vetiver, green mandarin, and cedar for a fresh take on its outdoorsy, earthy scent.” —KI.

Maison Francis Kurkdjian Oud Velvet Mood Extrait de Parfum.

Sources indicate that “For those who are oud-averse, Maison Francis Kurkdjian’s Oud Velvet Mood is a lighter iteration of the category. The oud has a woody quality, and when paired with spicy cinnamon, rich saffron, and juicy peach, the result is light and warm like the sun.” —KI.

“This stunning perfume is all gardenia and vanilla, and in its simplicity, it happens to be one of our most complimented scents of the year.” —JR.

Balenciaga Pink Oud Extrait de Parfum.

"This is a bold, long-wearing scent for those who live and die for the sensual pairing of rose and oud. We're obsessed with the way it blooms and evolves on skin throughout the night." —JR.

Ex Nihilo Demon Dancer Eau de Parfum.

“Ex Nihilo Demon Dancer feels like moving through the crisp air on a spring day, with peppermint providing a breezy contrast to juicy rhubarb, bright bergamot, and warm tonka bean.” —KI.

“We don’t know what we love more: the magnetic floral perfume that begs to be worn every day, the sculptural bottle, or the bookish packaging that made us a fan before we even took our first whiff.” —JR.

“You can’t go wrong with Beyoncé’s sultry and sophisticated hair perfume, which leaves hair with a long-wearing trail of bergamot, jasmine, oud, sandalwood, and Haitian vetiver.” —JR.

Creed Iris Debonair Eau de Parfum.

Sources indicate that “Delightfully unisex, this aromatic scent is a masterclass in balance. The top opens with bergamot, cardamom, pink pepper, and wormwood. In the middle, you’ll find fruity fig, lavender, and violet leaf. The base is iris, amberwood, and ambrette.” —JR.

Industry observers note that D.S. & Durga Resurrected Corpse Flower.

“Earthy and green, with an olive top note and banana base note—this is the perfume to buy this year if you want to smell wholly original and unabashedly cool.” —JR.

Sources indicate that “Creamy and warm with notes of chocolate and coffee, this is the must-have gourmand perfume of the winter. In a word, it makes us feel happy.” —JR.

Discothèque Next to Me or Nothing Eau De Parfum.

“More of a feeling than a fragrance, this scent is airy and easy to wear, with breezy notes of milk, jasmine, and woods.” —JR.

Phlur Heavy Cream Eau de Parfum.

"Gourmand lovers will want to overindulge in this elevated eau de parfum, which combines two types of creams—whipped and coconut—along with jasmine blossom and vanilla mousse notes for a sophisticated yet playful olfactory blend." —TDD.

“An olfactory version of a sound bath, Liis Forest Sounds boasts notes of bright yuzu, damp rain (earthier than plain water), green leaves, and woods.” —KI.

Dolce&Gabbana Dolce&Gabbana Your Devotion Eau de Parfum Intense.

Sources indicate that "The notes in this fragrance sound good enough to eat: Sicilian lemon, orange blossom, and vanilla milk. This is a date-night, delicious gourmand for those who usually prefer a lighter citrus scent." —JR.

Dries Van Noten Velvet Violet Eau de Parfum.

“This woody-gourmand scent captures the lush texture of velvet with a mix of unusual notes: violet leaf, clary sage essence, toasted sesame, barley roasted, and grilled tonka beans.” —JR.

Ellis Brooklyn Vanilla Rice Eau de Parfum.

Recent findings suggest that “Rather than wrapping yourself in a cashmere blanket on a cold day, try wearing Ellis Brooklyn’s Vanilla Rice. It combines the warm notes of toasted rice, cherry blossom, sweet vanilla, and creamy coconut milk for a soft, slightly floral scent.” —KI.

Estée Lauder Glimmer Eau de Parfum Spray.

“Estée Lauder’s Glimmer gives crisp orange flower and rose a warm finish with vanilla bean, tonka bean, amber, and two types of wood.” —KI.

Glossier You Soie Eau de Parfum.

“The latest addition to Glossier’s You fragrance lineup, Soie is an aquatic and solar take on a floral scent, with tropical Tiare flower water and creamy rice in place of powdery florals.” —KI.

“Not quite a fragrance, Future Society’s Base Scent is like the no-makeup makeup version of perfume. Infused with prebiotics and a patent-pending technology, the scent is designed to enhance and balance any fragrance layered beneath it—whether that’s lotion, deodorant, or your natural scent—by working with the skin’s microbiome.” —KI.

Harlem Perfume Co. Sensual Muse Eau de Parfum.

“A fruity floral that reads as more sophisticated, Harlem Fragrance Co.’s Sensual Muse gives juicy apricot, bright citrus, and creamy gardenia a warm, compelling character once whipped vanilla, sandalwood, and amber are added into the mix.” —KI.

“If you prefer your cocktails in fragrance form, look no further than By Kilian, which has mastered the art of turning a nutty, warm, slightly sweet espresso martini into a wearable scent that feels especially seductive at night.” —KI.

Shop our fave Black Friday Apple deals.

So, should you shop these record-low deals now or wait until Black Friday (November 27)? As a tech-obsessed editor who tracks these prices all year long, I’m sharing everything you need to know below.

Industry observers note that the best Apple Watch deal I’m seeing for Black Friday? The Apple Watch SE 3, which just returned to a record-low price of $199. It’s the most budget-friendly smartwatch in Apple’s lineup, but the S10 chip-powered device doesn’t skimp on premium features. There are tons of handy health insights to help you reach your fitness goals, from workout monitors that’ll count those 10,000 steps to sleep scores and even period cycle tracking.

This watch is available in 40mm or 44mm sizes, making it a great option if you prefer a sleeker look that won’t compete with your outfits. It also boasts up to 18 hours of battery life, with a fast-charging mode that’ll get you from 0 percent to 80 percent battery in just 45 minutes. Basically, this is your best option for a no-frills, entry-level smartwatch that won’t break the bank.

According to recent reports, if you’re looking for more in-depth fitness insights and faster processing, the brand-new Apple Watch Series 12 is also worth adding to cart while it’s on sale for its lowest price ever. It boasts the same safety features and fitness trackers as the SE 3, plus upgraded insights like a Blood Oxygen app and hypertension notifications.

The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is the largest and most premium model in Apple’s lineup, with a 49mm case size and S11 chip. Most impressive of all, it has the longest battery life of any Apple Watch—50 hours, to be exact—which is more than double the life of the SE 3 or Series 12. It’s right now out of stock, but it was on sale for a record-low price of $700 earlier this month.

Recent findings suggest that similarly, the Apple Watch Ultra 3 (2025) is currently sold out, but it was on sale for $549 a few weeks ago. This S10 chip-powered model offers health insights like heart rhythm reports, blood oxygen scoring, and sleep score tracking, as well as safety features like crash detection and emergency SOS. Plus, it boasts an impressive 42-hour battery life to boot.

My two cents? The Apple Watch SE 3 and Series 12 are the best models for most shoppers, and they’re finally at record-low prices. I recommend scooping them up now before they inevitably sell out—no need to wait until next week. However, if you prefer a high-tech model like the Ultra 3 or 4, I predict at least one will be back in stock soon.

40 Years On, the Musée des Arts Décoratifs’ Fashion Collection Remains Ahead of Its Time

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1184 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, on my first trip to France in the mid-2000s, the Musée des Arts Décoratifs (MAD) became my go-to destination in Paris for a fashion-museum fix.
  • This fall, the museum’s self-contained fashion collection—the Musée de la Mode et du Textile (originally Musée des Arts de la Mode)—celebrates its 40th anniversary with an exhibition titled “Look: 40 Years of Fashion at the Museum,” open through April 4, 2027.
  • “As the custodian of France’s National Fashion Collection, it was really notable for us to show people their heritage, as well as the diversity of the collection,” Sophie Lemahieu, the museum’s curator of fashion and textile collections after 1947, told Harper’s Bazaar.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, on my first trip to France in the mid-2000s, the Musée des Arts Décoratifs (MAD) became my go-to destination in Paris for a fashion-museum fix. With each subsequent visit, the intellectualized fashion scene became more saturated, as maisons increasingly invested in their heritage with public-facing venues (Fondation Azzedine Alaïa, Musée Yves Saint Laurent Paris, and Galerie Dior), plus the opening of Palais Galliera’s permanent galleries. As far as I’m concerned, when it comes to fashion exhibitions, the more the merrier. But I remain loyal to my first love. For art and design lovers like myself, it’s hard to top MAD’s interdisciplinary approach—and, of course, that prime Rue de Rivoli address.

This fall, the museum’s self-contained fashion collection—the Musée de la Mode et du Textile (originally Musée des Arts de la Mode)—celebrates its 40th anniversary with an exhibition titled “Look: 40 Years of Fashion at the Museum,” open through April 4, 2027. While the museum’s central hall, the Nef (“nave”), pays homage to 40 of its 70-plus highlights by spotlighting a look to represent each, the surrounding galleries invite visitors behind the scenes of an atelier and the museum itself.

“As the custodian of France’s National Fashion Collection, it was really notable for us to show people their heritage, as well as the diversity of the collection,” Sophie Lemahieu, the museum’s curator of fashion and textile collections after 1947, told Harper’s Bazaar. Co-curating the exhibition with MAD director Bénédicte Gady, Lemahieu sought to convey the skills of the many professionals who made each garment a reality, as well as the museum workers who care for and prepare them for display.

The multilayered approach represents a consecration of fashion as art—a concept MAD’s Musée de la Mode et du Textile has been instrumental in transmitting since its inception, when such a notion was far from the prevailing opinion. “40 years ago, it was not obvious to have fashion in the museum, even in Paris. There were many curators and art historians who were extremely mad because all these floors could have been used to show Islamic art or other decorative art collections,” noted Lemahieu. “It took time to legitimize fashion history as an art history field, but now every museum wants to have fashion exhibitions because they’ve seen how meaningful they can be. People identify with fashion because it’s part of our lives. We all wear clothes.”.

According to recent reports, for context, MAD was founded in 1864 and contained textiles and fashion prior to the official establishment of the Musée des Arts de la Mode. The decision to formalize its fashion collection was twofold: first, it marked the union of two monumental collections, the Union Centrale des Arts Décoratifs and the Union Française des Arts de la Costume. More broadly, during the 1980s, under President François Mitterrand, the French government began advocating for fashion as national cultural prestige, rather than a purely commercial entity (though it was undeniably one of the country’s leading exports). In 1982, the Louvre’s Cour Carrée courtyard became a designated venue for French ready-to-wear indicates, making a powerful global statement. To quote Lemahieu, “Fashion became political.”.

In a recent development, for the Musée des Arts de la Mode’s inaugural exhibition, “Moments de Mode” (1986)—which in “Look” is illustrated by a pristine 1760 robe à la française, the oldest garment in the show—MAD pulled out all the scenography stops. Working with theater professionals, curators presented an immersive history of fashion, including a mannequin, clad in a 19th-century cycling suit, in continuous movement on a mechanical bicycle. While today, such a display would never happen due to conservation requirements, it set the tone for MAD’s myriad innovations showcasing garments at their finest.

Another fascinating example from Moments de Mode is MAD’s usage of invisible mounts, which make garments appear as if they are floating. Visitors to Fondation Azzedine Alaïa may recall that these spectral mannequins have become somewhat of a signature for the institution. Lemahieu said this is not a coincidence: “Mr. Alaïa actually came to the exhibition in 1986 and thought this was an absolutely wonderful way to show a dress, so he asked the same person to do the mannequins for his foundation.”.

Recent findings suggest that elsewhere are odes to MAD’s many monographic shows, from its first, Yves Saint Laurent in 1986, to its traveling blockbuster “Christian Dior, Couturier of Dreams” in 2017. Dior is one of the few designers to have multiple MAD exhibitions—another is Schiaparelli, who was the subject of shows in 2004 and 2022. Similarly, MAD staged two exhibitions about the 1980s—in 1989 and 2022. Lemahieu noted in all cases, however, MAD never repeats its approach to the same subject.

She also pointed to several exhibitions conceived by her colleague, Denis Bruna, curator in chief of the Fashion and Textile Department, who favors a more sociological approach. “The Mechanics of Undergarments: An Indiscreet History of the Silhouette” (2013), for example, explored techniques used by women and men to shape their bodies, while “Proper Attire Required: When Clothing Causes a Scandal” (2016), focused on controversies that marked turning points in fashion history.

Sources indicate that nearly all the garments in “Look” were previously featured in their corresponding exhibitions. The one exception is a tricolor bodysuit that Gilles Asquin created for the 2024 Paris Olympics Opening Ceremony (several young designers contributed looks for the momentous event). The garment, which the French National Olympic and Sports Committee entrusted to MAD, is displayed to represent the exhibition “Fashion and Sport, From One Podium to Another,” 2023. Lemahieu remarked the bodysuit’s inclusion demonstrates how museum exhibitions can open pathways for future donations.

It has been revealed that acquisition, documentation, storage, conservation, and mannequinage (the art of mounting a garment) are some of the internal museum processes discussed in the “How Clothing Becomes a Work of Art: Backstage at the Museum” galleries. Meanwhile, “Backstage: Creating Couture” focuses on inspiration, fabrication, ornamentation, and photography. It’s here where MAD can proudly show the range of its holdings (more than 150,000 pieces from the third century to the present day), which include preparatory sketches, fashion illustrations, embroidery samples, and more. Rarities include a mannequin upon which Madeleine Vionnet draped her fabrics, as well as pleating boards used by Maison Lognon, a historic Parisian pleating atelier founded in 1853.

It has been revealed that running concurrently this fall at MAD are exhibitions dedicated to the Thai court’s fashion evolution, Brazilian photographer Rafael Pavarotti’s cutting-edge imagery, and Marion Delarue’s wearable art created during her residency at the museum. Forty years on, this mix of indicates, in scale and subject, has become MAD’s unique strength, as Lemahieu described: “It’s important for us to not just make bigger and bigger exhibitions. We need to be involved in what happens in haute couture, but we also need to be here for young designers and to be aware of what’s happening in fashion socially.” It’s that distinctive cocktail of programming—not to mention all the period-room interiors, jewels, and posters—that still keeps MAD at the top of my Paris museum list after all these years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that slather Greek yogurt and your favorite chili crisp on chicken thighs, roast in a hot oven, and you’ll be rewarded with juicy, tender meat with a delightful orange-tinged exterior. But the best part of this sheet-pan dinner comes after the chicken is cooked: Spread cooked rice into the pan’s juices, then slide the baking sheet back into the oven. As the rice soaks up the deeply savory sauce, it will crisp in spots, creating a texture that’s somewhere between chewy-fluffy steamed grains and a freshly toasted pita chip. And when it comes to chili crisp, we love the iconic and easy-to-source Lao Gan Ma, but specialty brands like Fly By Jing are great too—just make sure the one you use is not too spicy, which will overpower the dish.

More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.

Preheat oven to 425°. Season 6–8 skinless, boneless chicken thighs (1½–2 lb.) with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

Whisk together ¾ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt and ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. well-stirred chili crisp in a large bowl. Add chicken thighs and toss to coat.

Arrange chicken on a rimmed baking sheet and top with any yogurt mixture left in bowl. Bake chicken until deeply browned and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of a thigh registers 165°, 25–30 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board or plate.

Spread 3 cups cooked jasmine or short-grain rice over baking sheet with chicken juices and bake until most of the juices have been absorbed and rice is starting to crisp in spots, 12–15 minutes.

Meanwhile, whisk together 1 Tbsp. finely grated lime zest, ¼ cup fresh lime juice, ½ tsp. sugar, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt, and remaining ¼ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt in a small bowl.

Combine ½ medium head of green cabbage (about 1 lb.), very thinly sliced, and a substantial pinch of Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt in a large bowl. Using your hands, scrunch cabbage gently to soften. Add 1 small red onion, thinly sliced, 1 cup finely chopped cilantro, and yogurt dressing and toss to combine. Taste cabbage slaw and season with more salt if needed.

Slice chicken as desired and serve with crisped rice and cabbage slaw.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Superman actor David Corenswet, who’s set to reprise his Man of Steel role in Man of Tomorrow next year, just wore a way-out-of-left-field watch with a tuxedo during the 17th Governors Awards last night. There was no mistaking the glint of its dial from across the step-and-repeat: a Seiko ref. 6139 "Pogue" automatic chronograph. The bulky sport watch looked totally out of place in the restrained, elegant atmosphere of the awards ceremony…and absolutely perfect.

Sources indicate that the “Pogue,” as the yellow-dial variant is known, is a wildly cool and beloved watch, and Corenswet smartly took advantage of the way it pops against the black-and-white of a classic tux. Plus, it doesn’t hurt that among Seiko collectors, the Pogue is a cult classic, often ranking towards the top of best-Seiko-ever lists. Not only is it an aesthetic swerve on the red carpet, but it’s the type of relatively affordable oddball celebrities rarely reach for.

What’s so special about the 6139, and why is it called the “Pogue,” you might ask? The 6139 was among the very first batch of automatic chronographs. A group of brands—Seiko; a consortium of Hamilton-Büren, Heuer-Leonaids, Breitling, and Dubois Dépraz; and Zenith-Movado—raced to be the first to debut the mechanical innovation. Who won the race is still a matter of debate, but one thing is for certain: when the 6139 hit the Japanese market in 1969, it featured an integrated design, a column wheel, and a vertical clutch. Meshing hallmarks of classic chronograph construction with the convenience of automatic winding at a relatively affordable price, it was paired with a wide variety of colorful dials and funky cases and produced for roughly a decade.

A 1972 advertisement for the Pogue.

In a recent development, one of these designs, the ref. 6139-6002, is particularly eye-catching thanks to its bright-yellow dial with a contrasting blue-and-red tachymeter bezel, a 30-minute chronograph register, and a day-date display. American astronaut Col. William R. famously wore the Pogue during the Skylab 4 mission from November 1973 to February 1974. Subsequently, the 6139-6002 took on Pogue’s name, and is now one of the most collectible vintage Seiko references.

According to recent reports, the best part? Though there’s unfortunately no magic bullet to make you 6’4” and handsome as Superman, you can snag a pretty good “Pogue” for under $2,000. It may not take you into space, but as Corenswet has proven, it sure livens up your average black-tie outfit.

Since then, the couple has welcomed two kids together—Isabelle Amarachi, born in 2014, and Caleb Kelechi, born in 2016—and are seemingly thriving outside of the spotlight. But we think it’s time to learn a lil bit more about Nnamdi, don’t you?

Here’s everything you should know about the man behind Daddy Franklin, including how he rose to fame as a former NFL cornerback and what he’s up to next.

After growing up in Louisiana in a Nigerian Igbo household, Nnamdi attended the University of California, Berkeley, where he played for the California Golden Bears football team. Soon after graduating, Nnamdi was drafted in the first round of the 2003 NFL Draft by the Oakland Raiders, which is very impressive.

Over his 11-year professional football career, Nnamdi also played for the Philadelphia Eagles and the San Francisco 49ers, and in December 2013, the cornerback signed a one-day contract with Oakland so he could retire as a Raider. I love to see a loyal man!

According to recent reports, according to Nnamdi, the decision to retire at 32 was difficult, but it still felt like the right time for him. “Yeah, I felt that it was a good time, but it didn’t make it any easier,” he told UPROXX. “It’s a game that 'til this day I miss, and I miss playing. It’s not that I want to go play again, but I miss so many aspects of it; being around the team, being around the coaching, that calm before the storm.”.

Industry observers note that nnamdi first caught the acting bug all the way back in 2008, when he landed the role of “Party Guest with Wife” on the CW sitcom The Game. (Remember: There are no small roles, only small actors!!) He then caught the eye of director Peter Berg on the set of a Nike commercial shoot in 2009, who was impressed by the athlete’s ease in front of the camera. From there, Nnamdi went on to play small roles in Friday Night Lights, Leverage, and Cubed before making his on-screen feature film debut in 2012’s Fire with Fire.

According to recent reports, since retiring from the NFL, Nnamdi has fully committed himself to his acting career with starring roles in the films Crown Heights, Sylvie’s Love, The Good Nurse, The Knife, and—most recently—The Body. He’s also served as a producer on several of those projects as well.

In a recent development, despite all his success, Nnamdi still remains as modest as ever, avoiding social media and press to instead focus on his craft. “I’m really bad at self-promotion. It’s always been about team.”.

It has been revealed that during a 2018 interview with Today, Kerry corrected a host when they alluded to her two children, saying, “I’m a mother of three." And just like with Isabelle and Caleb, the couple keeps their eldest far from the paparazzi, so very little is known about her.

As Kerry joked to People, “I have moments where I take pictures or videos of one of my three amazing kids and I wanna post it online, and I tend to just send it to my parents or my shrink instead.”.

Philanthropy is notable to Nnamdi, which is why he created the Asomugha Foundation in 2005 at the very beginning of his career.

The foundation has two main programs: Orphans and Widows in Need (which provides food, shelter, medicine, vocational training, literacy efforts, and scholarships to widows and orphans in Nigeria) and Asomugha College Tour for Scholars (which takes selected students from Bay Area and Los Angeles area high schools on college tours across the country).

We’re very supportive of each other’s journeys, but we’ve always been that way. We always want the best for each other in whatever we’re doing.”.

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are plenty of ways to make a statement with your outerwear, from an oversize silhouette to a high collar or bold color.
  • Recent findings suggest that in particular, frog fastenings are having a resurgence, bringing a fanciful finishing touch to everything from minimalist wool peacoats to tailored military-inspired jackets.
  • Sources indicate that while they may seem latest for the season, frog-fastener jackets have a history that spans centuries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are plenty of ways to make a statement with your outerwear, from an oversize silhouette to a high collar or bold color. But this fall, designers are turning their attention to a smaller detail: the fastening. Jackets featuring decorative knots, elaborate loops, and ornate toggles have emerged as one of the season’s biggest outerwear trends, offering an alternative to standard buttons and zippers.

Recent findings suggest that in particular, frog fastenings are having a resurgence, bringing a fanciful finishing touch to everything from minimalist wool peacoats to tailored military-inspired jackets. Typically constructed from fabric or braided cord, the fasteners consist of a knotted button and a loop. Originally designed to secure garments, the closures have evolved into a more ornamental role with intricate shapes and floral-like designs.

Sources indicate that while they may seem latest for the season, frog-fastener jackets have a history that spans centuries. In Chinese dress, knotted closures known as pankou have long appeared on garments such as the qipao and tangzhuang. By the 18th and 19th centuries, frogging had also become a feature of European military uniforms, worn by cavalry regiments whose fitted jackets were adorned with braided cords.

Fashion has revisited the detail since then. Oscar de la Renta incorporated frog fastenings into his designs in the 1990s, while Valentino explored versions for its fall 2015 couture collection. More recently, for fall 2026, designers reinterpreted knotted closures: At Kallmeyer, black toggles punctuated a gilded jacquard jacket, while Kim Shui incorporated the detail into fur-trimmed blazers and opera jackets. Meanwhile, labels like Khaite and Ann Demeulemeester embraced military-inspired looks featuring ornamental braiding and embellished fronts.

Today’s store-rack versions range from collarless blazers with understated knots to dramatic outerwear designs featuring detailed cording. Brands like Róhe have introduced contemporary takes on frogging, while Hong Kong–based fashion label Sau Lee has reimagined traditional Tang-style jackets with modern silhouettes.

Rather than reinventing jackets entirely, designers are proving that something as minuscule as a fastening can make a familiar silhouette feel new again for the season. Ahead, shop our favorite takes on the look.

A chameleon both on and offscreen, Pamela Anderson proves short hair can be incredibly versatile and has made a strong case for trendy hairstyles that feel grown-up and sophisticated. The celebrated actress and former Bazaar UK cover star has experimented with sharp micro-bangs, gone auburn with a fluffy ’70s mullet, and embraced French glamour with a chic chignon. Her most recent look is understated and fresh, but with plenty of personality: the “soft wolf” cut.

The ’70s-inspired wolf cut is characterized by choppy layers with face-framing pieces that get gradually longer along the bottom, delivering plenty of volume and movement. It’s a cut that makes an impact all on its own and has personality in spades. Anderson’s version takes the wolf cut and gives it a polished, understated twist. A softer take on the trend, this chop feels effortlessly cool. “The benefit of a ‘soft wolf’ cut is that it allows a fashion-led hair shape to be kept feminine and ageless by softening the edges,” says Anita Rice, the cofounder of Buller and Rice salons. “It’s youthful yet chic.”.

In a recent development, according to Rice, it’s key to consider the length of hair that sits around the temples. “This is a crucial part of the hairline, and when cut shorter it can give a harder feel, but if you keep it longer and softer, it can create a more versatile, flattering silhouette,” Rice says. It works across all ages, but if your hair tends to be fine, avoid “over-texturizing,” which can make it look thinner and wispier.

In a recent development, adds Rice: “You still want to create softness, and this is about getting the right type of technique to encourage volume without leaving the hair feeling limp.” To style, wear it à la Anderson by gently pushing it back from the face, or experiment with a deep side part. “Alternatively, adding volume through a bouncy blow-dry with ‘flicky’ ends helps achieve a more ’70s feel.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is a Japanese-style rice porridge known as okayu. I ate this every morning in the early weeks of postpartum after my first daughter was born. It’s what our family reaches for whenever we need a simple, nourishing dish that warms from the inside out. For the smoothest porridge, let the rice soak in cold water before cooking.

If you have time, soak the rice, which makes the texture softer and can aid in digestion. Place washed rice in a bowl and pour in water to cover by 1". Soak at least 30 minutes and up to 4 hours. Drain off excess water before starting the recipe. The wakame seaweed, which you’ve probably had in miso soup, can typically be found dried anywhere Asian groceries are available.

In a recent development, in The Fourth Trimester, we ask parents: What meal nourished you after welcoming your baby? This month it’s a cozy rice porridge by Eating at Home cookbook author Trinity Mouzon Wofford. Read more: Breakfast at Home, After Birth at Home.

Recent findings suggest that combine 1 cup short-grain rice, washed, soaked if desired, ¼ cup dried wakame (seaweed), 1 Tbsp. dried red shiso, and 6 cups low-sodium broth (any kind) or water in a large donabe, medium Dutch oven, or other heavy pot. Cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat (you’ll hear bubbling). Uncover and stir, making sure nothing is stuck to bottom of pot. Cover and reduce heat to low. Continue to cook porridge 30 minutes more (resist the urge to peek).

It has been revealed that remove pot from heat and let porridge sit (still covered) 10 minutes. Uncover and stir. Rice grains should be cooked through, broken open, and creamy, but porridge should still be fairly loose. Season porridge with fine sea salt.

Ladle porridge into bowls and serve, topped with toasted sesame seeds, toasted sesame oil, and/or thinly sliced scallions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that menswear guys love Japanese denim. Menswear guys also love sneakers. So why not make some kicks for the people who can tell you exactly which artisanal mill produced their selvedge? That seems to be the thinking behind the latest Social Status x Air Jordan 1 Low OG ‘Sashiko.’.

It has been revealed that social Status is a North Carolina-based sneaker and streetwear boutique owned by the Whitaker Group, the same firm behind A Ma Maniére. Over the years, it’s worked with Nike on everything from milk-inspired Dunks to Air Pennys. The shop’s last proper Jordan collab was an extremely hairy Air Jordan 6 from 2019, but now the pair are back with something a little easier to wear.

Social Status x Air Jordan 1 Low OG ‘Sashiko’.

It has been revealed that social Status’s take on the AJ1 Low starts with the classic ‘Chicago’ color palette. The toebox is white, the overlays are red, and the Swoosh and collar are black. But rather than keeping everything box-fresh, Social Status has roughed up the leather so it arrives pre-scuffed, as though you’ve owned these shoes for years.

It has been revealed that the major switch happens across the sidewalls. The usual white leather panels have been replaced with mismatched patches of indigo fabric covered in white sashiko-style stitching. Sashiko is a traditional Japanese embroidery technique used to reinforce, repair, and extend the life of clothing. It’s particularly associated with vintage workwear and denim, which is why these Jordans look like they’ve been mended using a very expensive pair of jeans.

There’s also an old-school nylon tongue, a slightly aged sole, and a custom shoebox wrapped in the same blue pattern.

Social Status x Air Jordan 1 Low OG ‘Sashiko’.

Industry observers note that while you might normally expect this sort of significant Jordan release to land on the High, it’s nice to see the Low silhouette get some love. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Text by OdeImages by Ode and Maltoni.

CARRANCA draws on the eponymous sculptures, anthropomorphic and zoomorphic figures traditionally believed to ward off evil spirits, also associated with Afro-Brazilian religious traditions such as Candomblé. The project references Exu, the orisha who mediates between the material and spiritual worlds and is associated with movement and the creation of possibilities. Inspired by ancient Egyptian and Yoruba cultures, the carrancas’ physiognomy blends human and animal traits, evoking pre-dynastic Egyptian deities.

The palette of black, red, indigo, and white references these traditions and Brazilian popular representations of Exu. Using Afro-surrealism as a conceptual framework, the series visually narrates Urias’ eponymous album, with each photograph corresponding to a track. The project explores transcorporeality and how reclaiming divine and ancestral figures can become a means of liberation from Eurocentric identity norms.

Creative Director, Art Director and Stylist: OdePhotography: MaltoniSet Design: Jean LabancaHair and Makeup: Ivan BarriaUrias’ Hair: Rafaella SchlinUrias’ Makeup: Camila AnacNail Artist: CyshimiProduction: BELTRAME+Post-Production: Studio Bruno RezendeCast: Fina Cadjancu, Akin Henrias and Marcinha do Corintho.

Recent findings suggest that ode (b. 1998) is a Brazilian multidisciplinary artist working across filmmaking, creative direction, styling, writing, and curatorial practice. Her work explores self-representation as a means of challenging Eurocentric notions of identity through transcorporeality, Afro-Brazilian spirituality, memory, and transformation. Her photobooks and films, including A Rose and A Prayer (2022), Divina (2022), and CARRANCA (2025), bring human figures, deities, and Afro-surrealist narratives into dialogue. Her work has been exhibited at MEP, Instituto Moreira Salles, Lafayette Anticipations, ICA London, Photo London, and SP-Arte. She founded the platform Dúdús (2016–2019) and has curated exhibitions dedicated to Afro-diasporic art. Her work has been featured in Vogue, Dazed, ArtReview, and Harper’s Bazaar, and she has collaborated with Comme des Garçons, Jean Paul Gaultier, and COLORSxSTUDIOS.

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Recent findings suggest that one of the greatest things about the best kinds of jewelry is that it has no limits. Unlike clothing, it can pretty much be made out of anything, so long as it’s durable. Glass, in jewelry, dates as far back as around 3500 BCE in ancient Mesopotamia and Egypt, via beads and carvings. Yet all these years later, designers are revisiting the humble material, along with wood, porcelain, and beyond. It makes sense: We’re definitely in an era of experimental jewelry, and materials that push beyond the typical precious metals and gemstones allow for bolder shapes and silhouettes, with major impact. Enter: wooden pendants, glass rings, and porcelain chains.

On the runways recently, we’ve seen Chanel and Dries Van Noten toy with glass necklaces, Margiela play with porcelain (in the form of an ASMR-worthy dress that was an undercover nod to the house’s famous ’90s vest made of the material) as well as multilayered tidbits in standout pieces like Celine’s charm necklaces.

Likewise, fine jewelers are integrating various materials into their work. Marla Aaron, for instance, reimagined her Lock connector pendant in an official collaboration with Nymphenburg porcelain. Marie Lichtenberg makes beautiful dice pendants rendered in black ebony and diamonds. Anna Maccieri Rossi recently released an entire collection dedicated to wood, including chunky necklaces and carved bangles set with gemstones. “I love wood because it is a living material, warm and natural,” she remarked of the collection. “This material offers me the chance to dream and work on a large scale, with a bolder approach.”.

Industry observers note that the cost of gold rapidly ascended in 2025, reaching an all-time nominal record high of $5,589.38 per troy ounce in January 2026. Driven by historic market shifts and a broader surge in precious metal prices, this sharp economic rise has dramatically reshaped how fashion insiders, collectors, and everyday jewelry lovers approach their collections. As traditional solid gold pieces become increasingly rare financial splurges, buyers are actively diversifying their wardrobes with creative, tactile alternatives. In addition to gravitating toward vintage sterling silver and archival heirlooms, jewelry aficionados are now getting their fix with these alternative materials—ranging from hand-carved wood and delicate hand-blown glass to sculptural porcelain and unconventional metals.

Industry observers note that some designers, too, are looking to build and reinvent the legacy of those who came before them. “I think when most people hear ‘glass jewelry,’ a pretty specific image comes to mind,” Colin Keane Lynch of Keane Newly introduced York tells ELLE. “I’m interested in building on that history while exploring some of the less familiar possibilities.” Lynch, who has devoted his life to working with glass, designs sculptural glass petal rings and sinuous cuffs, all made to order. “Another thing I love about glass is its ability to take on the appearance of so many different materials through explorations of form, texture, and color. It also allows me to create things that might be difficult or even impossible to achieve in other materials.”.

Much like the language and energy of crystals and gemstones, others are interested in these materials because of what they represent. Take Thatch, for instance. Founded by Amy Goin and Laura Laing, the brand sells huge wooden heart pendants as well as fish-shaped wooden bangles and charms. “We feel that wood holds energy the same way gemstones do,” says Goin. “A different kind of energy. Something quieter and more grounded. It’s soulful and raw. We love the bohemian beauty of wood, paired with a touch of gold and sparkle.”.

For today’s designers, the most precious thing about jewelry is the possibility.

In a recent development, every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

If the late, great, legendary fashion editor Diana Vreeland were still alive, I believe she would incorporate a question like, “Why don’t you replace your ring stacks with statement gloves?” into her famous “Why don’t you” column, where she rhetorically mused on ridiculous and often opulent situations. A good glove is a winter staple, yes. But lately, fashion has been having a love affair with embellished, stylized gloves. We’ve now seen the opera glove in all of its forms. But what about gloves bedecked in crystal cuffs, neon hues, faux fur effects, and beyond? They’ve already arrived, on the runways and at retailers.

Consider Givenchy’s leather wonders, which come in ballooning silhouettes that envelop the hands and wrists. Or Prada’s spring/summer 2026 silky satin opera gloves in shades of pale yellow or olive green. With delicate ruching throughout, the formal opera glove gets an ironic, modern, slouched, and louche makeover. Elsewhere, Khaite has shown the power of an opera-length glove in python. Clearly, texture is an embellishment all its own in these kinds of extreme examples.

In some cases, the gloves become the jewelry. In others, jewelry further accents the statement glove, like for Mugler’s fall/winter 2026 show in which models wore kelly green and royal purple scrunched leather gloves up to their elbows, sometimes styled with a significant chunky bracelet over top. Elsewhere, some gloves were mismatched: vivid yellow on one hand and brilliant blue on the other. The brand called it a fresh take on power dressing, which melded codes of the 1980s, 1940s, and 17th-century aristocratic court coats. “Ultimately, this show intends to acknowledge that self-empowerment is the most potent antidote of clarity to the oppressive forces and grey political climate that surrounds us at this very moment,” Mugler creative director Castro Freitas was quoted in the show notes, “and most of all, it’s a manifesto of the highest power that we should never forget to reclaim: FREEDOM.”.

Recent findings suggest that most of all, the statement glove dresses up any neutral wool coat or adds an extra layer of over-the-top theatrics to a statement coat. When in doubt, you could also simply opt for a colorful glove, which the runways have loved in droves lately. Take, for example, Valentino, which has been pumping out short and statement-making silky gloves in shades of ’80s neon pink or dreamy cobalt blue.

According to recent reports, sometimes, all you need is a change of silhouette, too. At Chanel, the fingerless glove has long been a staple, and it’s now become a favorite of superfan clients during street style moments between reveals. Elsewhere, the fingerless glove has forever been a celeb favorite, especially when it comes to style legends like Madonna.

“We’ve got every color under the rainbow of gloves and/or a sheer opera-length glove that is in either a matching color or an opposite color of whatever the look is,” Madonna’s stylist Rita Melssen told ELLE in August 2026.

One thing is clear: Statement gloves are the new power accessory, equal parts practical, theatrical, and impossible to ignore.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joseph Zada is doing “very, very, very good,” he tells me, with a heavy emphasis on the third very and an audible exclamation mark. And why shouldn’t he be?

His much-anticipated film, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, finally comes out this week. Zada and I spoke the morning of his New York City premiere, while he was being shuttled from one press obligation to the next, already go-go-go before actually hitting the red carpet Monday night in custom Louis Vuitton, punctuated with a pair of gold-toed cowboy boots from Pharrell’s first collection for the brand.

In the film, Zada plays a young Haymitch Abernathy, who we follow through his own Hunger Games, some twenty-five years ahead of the events of the original trilogy. When asked about the movie, the 21-year-old Australian demonstrates palpable care and excitement, even a bit of sadness that it’s over. “I just think that it was the most I’ve had to prepare and the most support that I’ve had and the most that I’ve ever stepped into a character’s shoes,” Zada indicates. “And it was just such a joy to act in this and to feel what it was like to really be this character.”.

Since being cast, he’s barely had a second to stop and reflect on joining one of the biggest franchises in the world—and this comes right on the heels of East of Eden, too, in which Zada played another haunted young man. He laughs when I note the comparison: “I guess I just pride myself on my ability to show my vulnerability.”.

Below, read our full conversation with the emerging star as he reflects on his Hunger Games journey, talks red carpet style, and shares his thoughts on Robert Pattinson playing James Bond.

Joseph Zada: Yeah, I wonder if I’ll be nervous.

It has been revealed that maybe towards the start. It doesn’t get old… but it gets familiar.

Well, I did SiriusXM this morning, and then, I mean, it’s basically just been like, "Hey, do press all day and then go to your premiere." So there’s not much time for a ritual, so I guess I go a little bit nonverbal and half-dissociate.

Industry observers note that no, it’s so much fun. I have a lot of fun at these premieres. It’s always like a crazy, crazy crowd. The way they’ve set it up has just been otherworldly, and I’m not sure if I’ll ever have it again, but I distinctly remember each stop and the feelings that I’ve had thus far, and it doesn’t get old. It’s always crazy to see this many fans and the passion they have for this project. I mean, it’s not every day that you get to step into something with a built-in fan base where people are already coming out and supporting it before they’ve even seen it. So it’s a really special experience, and I don’t know when I’m going to be able to get that again.

It has been revealed that where did I have the most fun? I had a lot of fun in London because my little sister was there, my little sister and my brother’s girlfriend, so I got to hang out with them and I haven’t seen them in a while. And Mexico. Mexico was the craziest event that we’ve had. There were literally thousands, several thousands of people there. The reception was incredible.

Recent findings suggest that am I allowed to drop this? Oh, yes, that is what this [interview] is for. I’m wearing a Louis Vuitton suit—custom, custom—that Jason [Bolden] and I have worked together on, and I’m a big fan of the boots. The boots are pretty dope.

You know I have some serious stompers.

I feel a lot more comfortable in these clothes nowadays, and it’s actually become a lot more enjoyable to put them on. And it feels like more of an armor and less of a scary thing, and it feels like I build a lot of confidence being able to do this.

My red carpet style, I think... I don’t know. Just whatever Jason puts me in for the night.

Yeah, I think just doing it so often and finding different looks and just being able to wear all the different brands and find what I’m comfortable in.

According to recent reports, I pride myself on my ability to have vulnerability. I think as a young man, that’s what I find interesting in these performances of these young men coming of age, and I think that was really what I was just looking for in my early career. I modeled my career on people like Timothée Chalamet and Lucas Hedges, and I love the way that they kept their heart on their sleeve and how they feel like an open nerve. I love being able to portray that in my performances.

Recent findings suggest that I just think that it was the most I’ve had to prepare and the most support that I’ve had and the most that I’ve ever stepped into a character’s shoes and really, really felt like I was there every single day and just had the most incredible support in terms of my cast mates and my directors and my producers. And it was just such a joy to act in this and to feel what it was like to really be this character.

I guess everything just kind of changed just like that. Everything just changed in one quick second, and it feels like... I guess I haven’t really thought about what it was like before. Industry observers note that I’m just excited to be at home every single day and watch movies with my mom and my siblings and see all my friends. That’s what I’m really excited for. I’m just excited to also just turn off my phone for a little bit, maybe go on a little road trip down to South Australia and get a little beach house and not bring my phone and have six days where I’m just off the grid.

I feel like people ask me what was the best part of my year, and I just start naming all the movies that I’ve watched. Recent findings suggest that I think... I don’t know. I loved Wild Horse Nine. That’s a favorite I’ve watched in cinemas. I loved Primetime too, because I love Rob Pattinson. I love Skyler Gisondo.

I did just see the Bond casting news! I am chuffed. That is so exciting. That is beyond exciting. He is just the most phenomenal actor, and he really just makes the most interesting choices. And I think him in that role, the stoicism that he’ll bring along with those really interesting choices, it’s going to make that character so interesting. He’s a really special actor. I don’t know. It’s so ridiculously helpful to have a book with you because it’s just so much information, and I love preparing for roles and having a book because it’s just an internal monologue, which is what you should be doing for every character. You read a scene, and you should be writing what is going through your character’s head. And when you have a book, it’s all done for you, or at least you have a good foundation.

I hope I get to do as many book adaptations as possible, but I think what I’m really looking for is just a great director and a great script. I’m not sure what’s [next]. I’ve got a fresh slate right now, but there’s a couple of things floating around.

Latest Update: Apple Juice Bread

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level.
  • I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal.
  • Take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level. The subtle, but unmistakable, undercurrent of apple sweetness struck me as a bit of a magic trick in a bread that, otherwise, to the eye and hand was just a soft white loaf.

I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal. When I asked him what he did differently to prepare it, he noted he just took the same rustic bread recipe he baked elsewhere and used apple juice in place of water. I was incredulous. That was it? The same amount? The same technique? Yes and yes, he said. I was hooked. It turns out the water-to-juice switcheroo gives an added taste of fall without taking anything away from the shape and texture. It’s become an instant favorite at my house both breakfast and lunch, and I expect it will be at yours.

Take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed. You can do it!

More apple recipes here: 37 Apple Desserts That Make Us Want to Pick the Whole Orchard.

It has been revealed that mix 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, 1¾ cups apple juice, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.) in a large bowl just until flour is hydrated and a very shaggy dough forms, about 1 minute. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit at room temperature 15 minutes.

Set a small bowl of room-temperature water on work surface for easy reaching. Uncover dough, dip your hand in water and stretch one side of dough up and over to meet opposite side; turn bowl 90°. Repeat 3 more times, turning bowl 90° after each fold. (This constitutes 1 full fold.) If dough doesn’t always stretch to meet opposite side, just aim for the middle. Wet your hands and shake off excess water any time dough begins to feel sticky. Cover dough and let sit 30 minutes (set a timer). Repeat folding process to make 1 full fold. Re-cover and let dough sit another 30 minutes. Repeat folding process and resting one more time. By the last fold, dough should be significantly smoother and tighter.

Transfer dough to a generously floured surface, dust with flour, and shape into a tight ball. Dust dough with more flour. Dust a kitchen towel with flour and place inside a high-sided bowl to line. Arrange dough, seam side up, in bowl on top of towel. Tightly cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit in a warm spot until puffy, about 45 minutes.

In a recent development, place a rack in middle of oven, then set a large ovenproof Dutch oven with a lid on it; preheat oven to 400°. Place a 12" square of parchment paper on a flat surface. Cut a 2"-long slit in each corner toward the center. Very carefully, tip dough out onto center of parchment, trying your best not to deflate it or ruin its shape. (It’s easiest to place parchment on a flat plate so you can easily turn dough out of bowl.) Working very promptly and using a pair of kitchen shears lightly coated in vegetable oil, cut an X in center of bread. Remove pot from oven and very carefully lower dough into pot. Cover pot and return to oven.

Bake bread 35 minutes. Uncover pot, reduce oven temperature to 375°, and continue to bake bread until crust is deeply browned, 35–40 minutes more. Carefully tip loaf out onto a wire rack and let cool at least 1 hour before slicing.

Sources indicate that do Ahead: Bread can be baked 3 days ahead. Let cool completely; store airtight at room temperature.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that opening a boutique is a delicate exercise in materials and mood to bring its world to life in a physical space. So it makes sense that for Karin Soderlind, Kristina Tjader, and Sofia Wallenstam, the sisters and founders behind Stockholm-based Dagmar, their Alyssa Kapito-designed flagship became a strong point of reference. When Wallenstam, the brand’s creative director, went looking for inspiration for pre-spring ‘27, the debut collection from newly introduced design director Rachael Proud, formerly creative director of Raey, the two didn’t need to look further than the walls of its new shop.

According to recent reports, “When Rachel and I started to look at what the collection should be, we looked at our store,” Wallenstam shares with Vogue. In the flagship, a metal Jean Prouvé piece hangs on the wall alongside a handcrafted André Sornay sofa, and the tension between the two became the collection’s throughline. “The Prouvé piece on the wall is metal, quite hard, almost brutalist, and then we have this beautiful soft boucle sofa,” she says. “That was the meeting point, the hard versus the soft.”.

Industry observers note that launching November 19 alongside a fresh brand identity, the 130-piece pre-spring collection spans relaxed denim (a favorite of Wallenstam’s), sharp-shouldered tailoring, a croc pencil skirt, open-cut tanks, suede outerwear, and boots, much of it drawing on the textures and tones of the store. “We wanted to reuse the bouclé, not in the same way obviously, but that feeling of it,” Wallenstam says. The colors, too—the blacks, whites, and browns—feel representative of the Dagmar woman, Wallenstam adds.

The collection also marks a newly introduced chapter for the Dagmar woman, who Wallenstam describes as confident and living a busy, bustling life with a packed calendar. “She might go and have a school drop-off and go straight to a meeting, and then meet friends, go to a dinner,” she shares. “She wants to look smart and she wants to look cool at the same time.” With Proud on board, that approach is getting a little more edge, with roomier silhouettes and sharper shoulders at the forefront. It’s a bit more oversized than Dagmar has done in the past, with warmer tones integrated throughout. Wallenstam also pushes back on the notion of minimalism, so often pinned on Scandinavian fashion. “Of course, we have neutral tones, but it has heritage. It has a depth to it and a warmth to it.”.

In a recent development, as for how she and Proud approached the collection together, “When Rachel and I first sat down to discuss what the collection should be and how it should feel, we started immediately with the Dagmar woman and what’s key to her,” Wallenstam states. And the pencil skirt is where Proud’s influence really demonstrates. “You can really see the meeting point between Rachel and Dagmar in the pencil skirt,” she says. “It’s a very feminine product, but it has an elastic waist to make it more relaxed, and it’s in croco, which is a little bit harder in the material.” It’s the piece in the collection that will feel as comfortable at your desk as it does at dinner—a full expression of the upcoming Dagmar approach. It’s the Prouvé and the bouclé sofa all over again, translated into a single skirt. And of course, the same push and pull runs through the rest of the collection.

Prices range from $140 to $3,300, and Vogue readers can exclusively shop the collection on Dagmar for 24 hours, before its official launch on November 20; retailer drops on Net-a-Porter and Nordstrom to follow.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Our long international nightmare is finally over: two-time Meme of the Year nominee Robert Pattinson has been chosen as Daniel Craig’s James Bond successor, bringing an end to an exhausting series of “reports” and “leaks” about Amazon’s search for a new 007.
  • In the hands of another (read: more limited) actor, I’d never suggest such a risky swerve.
  • 20 years ago, Casino Royale was a refreshing reset and a crucial corrective to the overflowing ridiculousness of the Piece Brosnan era.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Our long international nightmare is finally over: two-time Meme of the Year nominee Robert Pattinson has been chosen as Daniel Craig’s James Bond successor, bringing an end to an exhausting series of “reports” and “leaks” about Amazon’s search for a new 007. Finally we can stop the debates and fan-casting and let Patts and Denis Villeneuve cook until they’re ready to present their new vision. But that would require a level of restraint that the internet doesn’t typically exercise. Immediately after the protracted process of casting Bond concluded, the internet moved on to naming its dream picks for Bond Girls and Bond Villains (sometimes, to brilliant effect.) I can’t say I have a dog in either fight, at least not right now. My Bond WishList is of a different magnitude altogether: can we make James Bond silly again? Just a little, even, 15 percent goofball?

In the hands of another (read: more limited) actor, I’d never suggest such a risky swerve. But the best thing about Pattinson is his range. Sure, if Villeneuve and co. want to render Bond as the stoic and taciturn gentleman he’s generally been this century, Rob has proven he can do that, as every Tenet truther has been gleefully preaching for the last 24 hours. But more often than not, Pattinson is keen to get weird, whether that’s going Full Freak, as he does in Primetime, or approaching certain archetypal parts with a silly, goofy mood (like his conniving suitor in The Odyssey). He can do a “voice” (Mickey 17), he can do scumbag grime (Good Time), he can do hapless screwball (The Drama). Why not make what’ll be his biggest role to date a little cocktail of all his best elements? (Okay, he can leave the Mickey 17 voice behind.).

20 years ago, Casino Royale was a refreshing reset and a crucial corrective to the overflowing ridiculousness of the Piece Brosnan era. But in the past two decades, the pendulum has swung back—the gritty reboot has become studios' stock-in-trade. I feel the same way about Batman; the actual risky choice would be to make something less like Nolan’s series that, instead, hewed a little closer to, say, Batman Forever, or even the gothic camp of Tim Burton’s two films.

Recent findings suggest that of course, Robert Pattinson was at the center of a Batman reboot as well, and the result was a movie that felt more like a spiritual cousin to David Fincher’s Se7en; audiences ate it up so much that the hunger for a sequel persists even after endless delays. When it comes to franchises as high-stakes as Batman or Bond, you can’t trust these increasingly sauceless execs to make anything but the basic choice. There’s no reason to expect Jeff Bezos isn’t texting Denis screenshots from Skyfall for reference from his megayacht at this very moment.

But if there’s anybody capable of putting a little English on the handle while still giving the mainstream what it wants, it’s Significant Bob Pattinson. He could easily make his James Bond a little off, or he could go full seductive cad who smiles like Neil Tenet, has a ki with Q, and charms women with some playful banter instead of simply brooding them into submission. I’m not looking for invisible cars and sharks with lasers, or a Lothario like Roger Moore who speaks in puns. All I’m asking is that we give camp a chance. Because ultimately, the most exciting thing Villeneuve and Pattinson can do to set their Bond apart would be to loosen him up a little.

Recent findings suggest that dean and Dan Caten set out to design a rebel aristocrat’s wardrobe for pre-fall. Rigorous military uniforms and tailored pieces clashed with punk and glam rock references. Often the designers used “callbacks from previous Dsquared2 collections” as a starting point.

Recent findings suggest that for menswear that meant a leather-effect coated biker jacket and ripped denim pants with rocker vibes. Workwear proposals with paint splatters were juxtaposed against pinstriped pants and blazers hybridized with components of other garments. Uniforms had a moment as well. A peacoat with gold buttons, a blue Napoleon jacket with contrasting red piping, and a red tuxedo jacket with black lapels were all in the mix, their severity softened by double shirts held together with safety pins or distressed knitwear. Brooches created from logo-ed keys and crystals completed the picture.

A “Kate Moss attitude” characterized the women’s looks, with outerwear taking center stage. Distressed denim jackets were reworked with couture-like balloon-shaped backs, while a red leather jacket became more sculptural thanks to a metal wire strategically placed inside the hems and the collar. The same effect was used on a peacoat with a fur hood. Napoleon jackets were turned out in denim, giving them an everyday aura that was undercut by the Victorian lingerie-inspired garments paired with them. The mashups could be spotted within women’s as well; see the tweed inserts applied to a canvas parka or the workwear blouson accented with the hems of a red puffer jacket.
